chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he was asked about breastfeeding (radāʿ), so he said: "That which becomes forbidden through breastfeeding is that which becomes forbidden through lineage."
ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect of breastfeeding on marriage prohibitions in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the marital prohibitions arising from breastfeeding (radāʿ) are identical in scope to those of blood lineage (nasab), a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding kinship. This hadith clarifies that the legal status of a wet-nurse and her children mirrors that of biological parents and siblings, ensuring consistency in the rules of mahram relationships. The ruling underscores the transformative power of nursing in creating permanent familial bonds equivalent to consanguinity.
